kinds.d: Dried edible fungi: porcini, shiitake, morels and wood ear, rehydrated before cooking.

x.d: Dried king bolete, flavour intensifies on drying; soak in hot water for about 20 minutes and keep the liquor. Fungo di Borgotaro has PGI for four Boletus species.

v.d: PGI covering B. edulis, aereus, aestivalis and pinophilus; much 'Italian' porcini is imported

x.d: Japanese and Chinese dried shiitake; donko (winter mushroom) is a high grade and huagu (flower mushroom) the most prized, grown in cooler temperatures.
Morels dried by hanging threaded caps in the sun; blanching is advised before cooking.
Chinese dried fungi sold shredded or whole, valued for texture; main species Auricularia heimuer and A. cornea.

kinds.d: Dried edible seaweed; fresh seaweed is in Fruit & Vegetables.

x.d: Dried red alga (Pyropia) pressed into sheets of about 18 × 20 cm; the top grade is first-harvest shin-nori from the Ariake Sea.
Brown kelp Undaria pinnatifida used in Japan and Korea, sold as dried leaves.
Brown alga Sargassum fusiforme sold dried.
Red alga Palmaria palmata eaten dried as flakes or leaves, a source of iodine and protein.
Kelp Saccharina japonica; dried kombu for stock is covered with its varieties under Dashi and dashi ingredients.

kinds.d: Tomatoes dried in the sun or by machine, sold dry or packed in sunflower or olive oil.

notes: Koshin grade, morel and hijiki grades not on retrieved pages (koshin omitted; hijiki and Wakame (Naruto) origin not confirmed so no origin claim). Kombu is cross-linked to the dashi kind on shelf 05_02. No brands in register (Tangxiu, Yutaka are old-data models only). Dried mushroom and seaweed old sources kept.
